16|  standoffs, harness clips) for its smallsat bus **"Petrel"** (programmes Petrel-1, Petrel-2).

18|  the AI design assistant runs on one in-house GPU ("on-prem"), which is the Forge story.
19|- Small team (fictional): Structures, Avionics Integration, Quality. Engineers file **design requests** like
20|  "BRK-0412: base plate 60 × 40 × 4, four KF-M4 clearance holes 6 mm in from each corner, north wall 25 high".

23|Design goals: (a) clearly different from CadQuery (names, datum, tables), so knowing CadQuery is not enough;
24|(b) small and fully documented in the manual; (c) every Keel program becomes exactly one CadQuery solid;
25|(d) deterministic, no randomness.
26|

29|  +Z = "up". Nothing is centred unless the call says so.

37||---|---|---|

39|| KF-M3 | 3.4 | 6.5 × 3.0 |
40|| KF-M4 | 4.5 | 8.0 × 4.0 |
41|| KF-M5 | 5.5 | 10.0 × 5.0 |

47|import keel
48|p = keel.part("BRK-0412", material="AL6061")       # material is metadata only
49|p.stock(L, W, T)                 # base block: x∈[0,L], y∈[0,W], z∈[0,T]. Exactly one per part, first call.
50|p.wall(edge, h, t=None)          # wall standing on the top face along a named edge, flush with that edge,

53|p.hole(code, at=(x, y))          # through hole (all the way down) using table KF; "-CB" adds the counterbore
54|p.pocket(at=(x, y), L, W, depth) # rectangular pocket from the top face; (x, y) = pocket's lower-left corner
55|p.slot(at=(x1, y1), to=(x2, y2), width, depth="thru")  # straight slot with round ends, centre line x1,y1→x2,y2

86|   wrong shape, wrong position, error).

88|   Glimmer, teacher Spark Open) on the held-out exam, training status, cost. Shows "not measured yet" until results

93|  against itself PASS, and two deliberately wrong versions per example FAIL.

101|teacher run, training. Budget for this build: one Muse Code session, ~$0.50–0.80 Meta credit, user approval first.
102|

104|
105|# Keel v2: realistic company tool (SPEC addendum, 2026-10-28 ~23:30, user: "do it more realistic")
106|
107|Why: v1 is close to plain CAD; a small model with the manual may already do well, leaving Forge nothing to improve.
108|Real internal tools carry company knowledge: named standards, rules that depend on material and part class, family-
109|specific drawing conventions, and traps in the order of operations. v2 adds these. Everything stays exactly
110|checkable (each program still compiles to exactly one CadQuery solid) and fully documented in the manual: nothing
111|is secret from a careful reader, but a lot must be remembered and combined.
112|All v1 calls keep working unchanged. Version 2.0.0.
113|
114|## V2.1 Materials (changes the shape through the standards)
115|`keel.part(number, material="AL6061", cls="GSE")`. Material now matters:
116|| Material | Standard wall | Standard fillet | Minimum wall (KeelError if thinner) |
117||---|---|---|---|
118|| AL6061 | 2.5 | 1.0 | 1.5 |
119|| TI6AL4V | 3.0 | 1.5 | 2.0 |
120|| SS316 | 2.0 | 0.5 | 1.2 |
121|Unknown material → KeelError listing the three codes.
122|
123|## V2.2 Part class
124|`cls="GSE"` (ground support equipment, default) or `cls="FLIGHT"` (flies on the satellite). FLIGHT rules:
125|1. `finish()` applies the material's standard fillet to the stock's vertical edges automatically if `fillet()` was
126|   not called (an explicit `fillet(r=...)` wins).
127|2. Every fastener hole on the base must be counterbored (`-CB`) or countersunk (`-CS`); a plain code raises
128|   `KeelError: flight parts need -CB or -CS fasteners (KF-M4 at (x, y))`. Wall holes (V2.4) are exempt.
129|
130|## V2.3 Countersinks
131|Suffix `-CS`: 90° countersink from the local top (same "local top" rule as counterbores). Table KF gains a column:
132|| Code | Countersink Ø at the top |
133||---|---|
134|| KF-M2 | 4.3 |
135|| KF-M3 | 6.3 |
136|| KF-M4 | 8.4 |
137|| KF-M5 | 10.4 |
138|| KF-M6 | 12.4 |
139|Geometry: a cone from the countersink Ø at the local top narrowing at 45° (half-angle) down to the clearance Ø, then
140|the through hole.
141|
142|## V2.4 Holes in walls
143|`p.wall_hole(edge, code, at=(u, z))`: a plain KF clearance hole drilled horizontally through the wall on `edge`,
144|perpendicular to the wall, all the way through its thickness. `u` = distance along the wall: from the **west end**
145|for north and south walls, from the **south end** for east and west walls. `z` = height of the hole centre **above
146|the stock top**. KeelError if there is no wall on that edge, if the code has -CB/-CS, or if the hole does not fit
147|inside the wall (hole edge closer than 0 to the wall's top or ends).
148|
149|## V2.5 Company standard mounts
150|`p.mount(name, origin=(x, y), finish="plain")`, `finish` = "plain", "CB" or "CS" (applied to every hole of the
151|mount; FLIGHT rule 2 applies). Hole offsets are from `origin`:
152|| Name | Fastener | Holes (offsets from origin) |
153||---|---|---|
154|| PETREL-MOUNT-A | KF-M4 | (0,0), (40,0), (0,30), (40,30); origin = the south-west hole |
155|| PETREL-MOUNT-B | KF-M5 | (0,0), (60,0), (0,40), (60,40); origin = the south-west hole |
156|| STAR-TRACKER-3 | KF-M3 | 3 holes on a circle of diameter 30 around the origin, at 90°, 210° and 330° (0° = east, counter-clockwise) |
157|| HARNESS-P2 | KF-M2 | (0,0), (15,0); origin = the west hole |
158|`mount()` counts as one feature for `pattern()` (the whole mount is repeated) and for `mirror()`.
159|
160|## V2.6 Mirror
161|`p.mirror(axis)`: `axis="ew"` copies every hole, boss, pocket, slot and mount recorded so far to the mirror position
162|about the stock's centre line x = L/2; `axis="ns"` about y = W/2. Originals stay. Walls and wall holes are not
163|mirrored. After a mirror, `pattern()` raises KeelError (nothing to repeat).
164|
165|## V2.7 Reading design requests (manual section; a drawing convention, not code)
166|- BRK, PLT, STD and CLP requests give positions from the datum corner (as in v1).
167|- **FRM requests are dimensioned from the frame centre** (x east, y north, can be negative), because frames are
168|  symmetric. Keel always uses the corner datum, so convert: x = L/2 + x_request, y = W/2 + y_request.
169|- "Flight part" in a request means `cls="FLIGHT"`. A material named in a request (e.g. "titanium" = TI6AL4V,
170|  "stainless" = SS316, "aluminium" = AL6061) must be passed as `material=`.
171|
172|## V2.8 Build changes (for Muse Code)
173|- Library v2.0.0 in `company/keel/` (keep v1 behaviour for v1 calls; KeelError messages company-style).
174|- Manual v2 in `company/manual.md`: add sections for V2.1–V2.7 with one example each, plus 2 new worked examples
175|  that combine several rules. Target ≤ 6,000 tokens. It must contain no exam job (exam part numbers are in the
176|  BRK-2xxx…5xxx range and must not be used in the manual or examples; use 0xxx–1xxx numbers).
177|- Examples: keep the 8; add 4 v2 examples (a FLIGHT titanium bracket with a wall hole, a frame dimensioned from the
178|  centre with a mirror, a plate with PETREL-MOUNT-A countersunk, a stainless part with STAR-TRACKER-3).
179|- `company/selftest.py`: extend to every new rule (each error case, each mount, the auto fillet, the countersink
180|  cone, wall_hole positions, mirror). Use the Keel-exam referee tolerance (0.01%: import
181|  `experiments/keel-exam/referee.py`) for the wrong-variant checks.
182|- Dashboard: Keel v2.0.0; new cards/tables for Materials, Part classes, Standard mounts; Gauge card says overlap
183|  0.01%; label request statuses as "sample data" until real results exist.

121|Unknown material → KeelError listing the three codes.
122|
123|## V2.2 Part class
124|`cls="GSE"` (ground support equipment, default) or `cls="FLIGHT"` (flies on the satellite). FLIGHT rules:
125|1. `finish()` applies the material's standard fillet to the stock's vertical edges automatically if `fillet()` was
126|   not called (an explicit `fillet(r=...)` wins).
127|2. Every fastener hole on the base must be counterbored (`-CB`) or countersunk (`-CS`); a plain code raises
128|   `KeelError: flight parts need -CB or -CS fasteners (KF-M4 at (x, y))`. Wall holes (V2.4) are exempt.
129|
130|## V2.3 Countersinks
131|Suffix `-CS`: 90° countersink from the local top (same "local top" rule as counterbores). Table KF gains a column:
132|| Code | Countersink Ø at the top |
133||---|---|
134|| KF-M2 | 4.3 |
135|| KF-M3 | 6.3 |
136|| KF-M4 | 8.4 |
137|| KF-M5 | 10.4 |
138|| KF-M6 | 12.4 |
139|Geometry: a cone from the countersink Ø at the local top narrowing at 45° (half-angle) down to the clearance Ø, then
140|the through hole.
141|
142|## V2.4 Holes in walls
143|`p.wall_hole(edge, code, at=(u, z))`: a plain KF clearance hole drilled horizontally through the wall on `edge`,
144|perpendicular to the wall, all the way through its thickness. `u` = distance along the wall: from the **west end**
145|for north and south walls, from the **south end** for east and west walls. `z` = height of the hole centre **above
146|the stock top**. KeelError if there is no wall on that edge, if the code has -CB/-CS, or if the hole does not fit
147|inside the wall (hole edge closer than 0 to the wall's top or ends).
148|
149|## V2.5 Company standard mounts
150|`p.mount(name, origin=(x, y), finish="plain")`, `finish` = "plain", "CB" or "CS" (applied to every hole of the
151|mount; FLIGHT rule 2 applies). Hole offsets are from `origin`:
152|| Name | Fastener | Holes (offsets from origin) |
153||---|---|---|
154|| PETREL-MOUNT-A | KF-M4 | (0,0), (40,0), (0,30), (40,30); origin = the south-west hole |
155|| PETREL-MOUNT-B | KF-M5 | (0,0), (60,0), (0,40), (60,40); origin = the south-west hole |
156|| STAR-TRACKER-3 | KF-M3 | 3 holes on a circle of diameter 30 around the origin, at 90°, 210° and 330° (0° = east, counter-clockwise) |
157|| HARNESS-P2 | KF-M2 | (0,0), (15,0); origin = the west hole |
158|`mount()` counts as one feature for `pattern()` (the whole mount is repeated) and for `mirror()`.
159|
160|## V2.6 Mirror
161|`p.mirror(axis)`: `axis="ew"` copies every hole, boss, pocket, slot and mount recorded so far to the mirror position
162|about the stock's centre line x = L/2; `axis="ns"` about y = W/2. Originals stay. Walls and wall holes are not
163|mirrored. After a mirror, `pattern()` raises KeelError (nothing to repeat).
164|
165|## V2.7 Reading design requests (manual section; a drawing convention, not code)
166|- BRK, PLT, STD and CLP requests give positions from the datum corner (as in v1).
167|- **FRM requests are dimensioned from the frame centre** (x east, y north, can be negative), because frames are
168|  symmetric. Keel always uses the corner datum, so convert: x = L/2 + x_request, y = W/2 + y_request.
169|- "Flight part" in a request means `cls="FLIGHT"`. A material named in a request (e.g. "titanium" = TI6AL4V,
170|  "stainless" = SS316, "aluminium" = AL6061) must be passed as `material=`.
171|
172|## V2.8 Build changes (for Muse Code)
173|- Library v2.0.0 in `company/keel/` (keep v1 behaviour for v1 calls; KeelError messages company-style).
174|- Manual v2 in `company/manual.md`: add sections for V2.1–V2.7 with one example each, plus 2 new worked examples
175|  that combine several rules. Target ≤ 6,000 tokens. It must contain no exam job (exam part numbers are in the
176|  BRK-2xxx…5xxx range and must not be used in the manual or examples; use 0xxx–1xxx numbers).
177|- Examples: keep the 8; add 4 v2 examples (a FLIGHT titanium bracket with a wall hole, a frame dimensioned from the
178|  centre with a mirror, a plate with PETREL-MOUNT-A countersunk, a stainless part with STAR-TRACKER-3).
179|- `company/selftest.py`: extend to every new rule (each error case, each mount, the auto fillet, the countersink
180|  cone, wall_hole positions, mirror). Use the Keel-exam referee tolerance (0.01%: import
181|  `experiments/keel-exam/referee.py`) for the wrong-variant checks.
182|- Dashboard: Keel v2.0.0; new cards/tables for Materials, Part classes, Standard mounts; Gauge card says overlap
183|  0.01%; label request statuses as "sample data" until real results exist.

1|# Keel manual (internal wiki)
2|
3|*Quillon Orbital Works · Structures team · Keel v1.0.0 · QX-2 controlled: on-prem only.*
4|*Fictional company, made for the Forge demo.*
5|
6|Keel is our small internal tool for describing machined satellite parts in Python.
7|A Keel program is a short recipe: start from a base block, add walls and bosses,
8|cut holes, pockets and slots, and finish with exactly one solid. Keel compiles
9|the recipe to a solid model internally, and the Gauge station checks the result
10|against the design request. If you can write the recipe, you can make the part.
11|
12|## 1. Conventions (read this first)
13|
14|All dimensions are millimetres. The datum is the part's **lower-left-bottom
15|corner** at (0, 0, 0): +X points east, +Y points north, +Z points up. Nothing is
16|centred unless the call says so; every position is measured from the datum.
17|
18|The four edges of the base stock have names: **north** (+Y side), **south**
19|(−Y side), **east** (+X side), **west** (−X side).
20|
21|Holes never use raw diameters. Always use a **company fastener code** from
22|table KF below; the Gauge station checks the exact diameters, so a 4 mm drill
23|where a KF-M4 belongs will FAIL the part.
24|
25|Two company standards apply whenever a request says "standard": wall thickness
26|**2.5 mm**, fillet radius **1.0 mm**.
27|
28|Part numbers tell you the family: BRK (bracket), PLT (plate), FRM (frame),
29|STD (standoff), CLP (clip). The `material=` argument (default `AL6061`) is
30|metadata only and never changes the shape.
31|
32|A program has a fixed shape: one `stock()` call first, then features, then
33|`p.finish()` last. `finish()` returns the single solid.
34|
35|## 2. Fastener table KF
36|
37|| Code  | Clearance hole Ø | Counterbore Ø × depth |
38||-------|------------------|-----------------------|
39|| KF-M2 | 2.4              | 4.4 × 2.0             |
40|| KF-M3 | 3.4              | 6.5 × 3.0             |
41|| KF-M4 | 4.5              | 8.0 × 4.0             |
42|| KF-M5 | 5.5              | 10.0 × 5.0            |
43|| KF-M6 | 6.6              | 11.0 × 6.0            |
44|
45|Suffix `-CB` means counterbored from the top face, e.g. `KF-M4-CB`.
46|
47|## 3. API
48|
49|```python
50|import keel
51|p = keel.part("BRK-0412", material="AL6061")
52|```
53|
54|**stock(L, W, T)** — the base block, x in [0, L], y in [0, W], z in [0, T].
55|Exactly one per part, and it must be the first call.
56|
57|```python
58|p.stock(60, 40, 4)
59|```
60|
61|**wall(edge, h, t=None)** — a wall standing on the top face along a named
62|edge (`north`, `south`, `east`, `west`). It sits flush with that edge, runs the
63|full edge length, and rises `h` above the stock top. `t` defaults to the
64|standard wall of 2.5.
65|
66|```python
67|p.wall("north", 25)
68|```
69|
70|**boss(at=(x, y), dia, h)** — a cylinder on the top face centred at (x, y),
71|`h` high.
72|
73|```python
74|p.boss(at=(15, 15), dia=12, h=10)
75|```
76|
77|**hole(code, at=(x, y))** — a through hole, all the way down, using a KF code.
78|A `-CB` code adds the counterbore from the top face.
79|
80|```python
81|p.hole("KF-M4-CB", at=(8, 8))
82|```
83|
84|**pocket(at=(x, y), L, W, depth)** — a rectangular pocket cut from the top
85|face. (x, y) is the pocket's lower-left corner; `depth` must be less than the
86|stock thickness.
87|
88|```python
89|p.pocket(at=(10, 10), L=80, W=60, depth=4)
90|```
91|
92|**slot(at=(x1, y1), to=(x2, y2), width, depth="thru")** — a straight slot with
93|round ends along the centre line from start to end. `depth="thru"` cuts all the
94|way through; a number cuts a blind slot that deep from the top face.
95|
96|```python
97|p.slot(at=(10, 15), to=(40, 15), width=5)
98|```
99|
100|**pattern(nx, ny, dx, dy)** — repeats the LAST feature call in a grid, `nx`
101|by `ny` positions spaced `dx`, `dy` apart. The total is nx × ny instances
102|including the original call's position. Only boss, hole, pocket and slot can
103|be patterned. (A leading text label, e.g. `pattern("hole", 2, 2, 48, 28)`, is
104|accepted and ignored.)
105|
106|```python
107|p.hole("KF-M4", at=(6, 6))
108|p.pattern(2, 2, 48, 28)
109|```
110|
111|**fillet(edges="vertical", r=None)** — rounds the stock's 4 vertical outer
112|edges. `r` defaults to the standard fillet of 1.0. Only `edges="vertical"`
113|exists.
114|
115|```python
116|p.fillet()
117|```
118|
119|**finish()** — returns the part as exactly one solid. Must be the last call;
120|every program ends with `solid = p.finish()`.
121|
122|```python
123|solid = p.finish()
124|```
125|
126|**keel.render(p, path)** — writes an SVG preview of a finished part for the
127|dashboard catalogue. It needs a finished part, so call it after `finish()`.
128|
129|```python
130|keel.render(p, "brk_0101.svg")
131|```
132|
133|## 4. Error messages
134|
135|Keel errors are plain sentences starting with `keel:`. The common ones:
136|
137|- `keel: unknown fastener code 'M4'; holes use company codes KF-M2 ...` — you
138|  used a raw size instead of a KF code.
139|- `keel: stock() called twice; a part has exactly one base block ...` — delete
140|  the second `stock()`.
141|- `keel: hole() called before stock(); every part starts with p.stock(L, W, T)`
142|  — `stock()` must be the first call.
143|- `keel: unknown edge 'top'; edges are named 'north', 'south', 'east' or 'west'`.
144|- `keel: pattern() with no previous feature; call a feature first`.
145|- `keel: render() before p.finish(); finish the part first ...`.
146|
147|## 5. Worked examples
148|
149|L-bracket, 60 × 40 base with a north wall and four corner holes:
150|
151|```python
152|import keel
153|p = keel.part("BRK-0101", material="AL6061")
154|p.stock(60, 40, 4)
155|p.wall("north", 25)
156|p.hole("KF-M4", at=(6, 6))
157|p.pattern(2, 2, 48, 28)
158|p.fillet()
159|solid = p.finish()
160|```
161|
162|Standoff: a foot with a centre boss, drilled through the boss:
163|
164|```python
165|import keel
166|p = keel.part("STD-0044", material="AL6061")
167|p.stock(30, 30, 4)
168|p.boss(at=(15, 15), dia=12, h=10)
169|p.hole("KF-M4", at=(15, 15))
170|p.hole("KF-M3", at=(5, 5))
171|p.pattern(2, 2, 20, 20)
172|solid = p.finish()
173|```
174|
175|Clip with a through slot and an end wall:
176|
177|```python
178|import keel
179|p = keel.part("CLP-0012", material="AL6061")
180|p.stock(50, 30, 4)
181|p.slot(at=(10, 15), to=(40, 15), width=5)
182|p.wall("west", 10)
183|p.hole("KF-M3", at=(45, 8))
184|p.pattern(1, 2, 0, 14)
185|solid = p.finish()
186|```
187|
188|New here? Copy one example, change the numbers to match your design request,
189|and run it through the Gauge station before ordering metal.

106|        self._ops.append(op)
107|        self._seed = op
108|        return self

110|    def boss(self, at, dia, h):
111|        """Cylinder on the top face, centre at (x, y)."""
112|        self._guard_open("boss()")
113|        self._need_stock("boss()")
114|        (x, y) = at
115|        self._check_xy(x, y, "boss()")
116|        dia = _positive(dia, "boss diameter")
117|        h = _positive(h, "boss height")
118|        op = ("boss", {"at": (float(x), float(y)), "dia": dia, "h": h})
119|        self._ops.append(op)

121|        return self

123|    def hole(self, code, at):
124|        """Through hole (all the way down) using table KF; '-CB' adds the counterbore."""
125|        self._guard_open("hole()")
126|        self._need_stock("hole()")
127|        base = code[:-3] if code.endswith("-CB") else code
128|        if base not in KF:
129|            raise KeelError(
130|                f"keel: unknown fastener code {code!r}; "
131|                "holes use company codes KF-M2, KF-M3, KF-M4, KF-M5, KF-M6 "
132|                "(add -CB for a counterbore, e.g. KF-M4-CB)"
133|            )
134|        (x, y) = at
135|        self._check_xy(x, y, f"hole({code})")
136|        op = ("hole", {"code": code, "at": (float(x), float(y))})
137|        self._ops.append(op)
138|        self._seed = op
139|        return self

141|    def pocket(self, at, L, W, depth):
142|        """Rectangular pocket from the top face; (x, y) = pocket's lower-left corner."""
143|        self._guard_open("pocket()")
144|        self._need_stock("pocket()")
145|        (x, y) = at
146|        L = _positive(L, "pocket length")
147|        W = _positive(W, "pocket width")
148|        depth = _positive(depth, "pocket depth")
149|        SL, SW, ST = self._stock
150|        if not (0 <= x and 0 <= y and x + L <= SL and y + W <= SW):
151|            raise KeelError(
152|                f"keel: pocket at ({x}, {y}) size {L:g} x {W:g} does not fit "
153|                f"the {SL:g} x {SW:g} stock footprint"
154|            )
155|        if depth >= ST:
156|            raise KeelError(
157|                f"keel: pocket depth {depth:g} must be less than the stock thickness {ST:g}; "
158|                "use slot(depth='thru') for a cut all the way through"
159|            )
160|        op = ("pocket", {"at": (float(x), float(y)), "L": L, "W": W, "depth": depth})
161|        self._ops.append(op)
162|        self._seed = op
163|        return self

165|    def slot(self, at, to, width, depth="thru"):
166|        """Straight slot with round ends, centre line (x1,y1) -> (x2,y2)."""
167|        self._guard_open("slot()")
168|        self._need_stock("slot()")
169|        (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = at, to
170|        self._check_xy(x1, y1, "slot() start")
171|        self._check_xy(x2, y2, "slot() end")
172|        width = _positive(width, "slot width")
173|        if isinstance(depth, str):
174|            if depth != "thru":
175|                raise KeelError(
176|                    f"keel: unknown slot depth {depth!r}; use 'thru' or a depth in millimetres"
177|                )
178|        else:
179|            depth = _positive(depth, "slot depth")
180|            if depth >= self._stock[2]:
181|                raise KeelError(
182|                    f"keel: slot depth {depth:g} must be less than the stock thickness "
183|                    f"{self._stock[2]:g}; use depth='thru' for a cut all the way through"
184|                )
185|        op = ("slot", {"at": (float(x1), float(y1)), "to": (float(x2), float(y2)),
186|                       "width": width, "depth": depth})
187|        self._ops.append(op)
188|        self._seed = op
189|        return self

191|    def pattern(self, *args):
192|        """Repeat the LAST feature call nx x ny times with spacing dx, dy.
193|
194|        Total instances = nx * ny including the seed position, at
195|        (x + i*dx, y + j*dy) for i in 0..nx-1, j in 0..ny-1.
196|        A leading string label (e.g. pattern("hole", 2, 2, ...)) is accepted
197|        and ignored, for compatibility with the SPEC draft form.
198|        """
199|        self._guard_open("pattern()")
200|        self._need_stock("pattern()")
201|        if args and isinstance(args[0], str):
202|            args = args[1:]
203|        if len(args) != 4:
204|            raise KeelError(
205|                f"keel: pattern() takes (nx, ny, dx, dy), got {len(args)} arguments; "
206|                "it repeats the LAST feature call"
207|            )
208|        nx, ny, dx, dy = args
209|        if self._seed is None:
210|            raise KeelError("keel: pattern() with no previous feature; call a feature first")
211|        if self._seed[0] in ("wall",):
212|            raise KeelError(
213|                f"keel: pattern() cannot repeat {self._seed[0]}(); "
214|                "only boss, hole, pocket and slot can be patterned"
215|            )
216|        for name, value in (("nx", nx), ("ny", ny)):
217|            if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool) or value < 1:
218|                raise KeelError(f"keel: pattern {name} must be a positive whole number, got {value!r}")
219|        kind, params = self._seed
220|        for i in range(nx):
221|            for j in range(ny):
222|                if i == 0 and j == 0:
223|                    continue  # the seed call itself
224|                moved = dict(params)
225|                if kind in ("boss", "hole"):
226|                    x, y = params["at"]
227|                    moved["at"] = (x + i * dx, y + j * dy)
228|                    self._check_xy(*moved["at"], f"pattern() copy of {kind}()")
229|                elif kind == "pocket":
230|                    x, y = params["at"]
231|                    moved["at"] = (x + i * dx, y + j * dy)
232|                    px, py = moved["at"]
233|                    SL, SW, _ = self._stock
234|                    if not (0 <= px and 0 <= py and px + params["L"] <= SL and py + params["W"] <= SW):
235|                        raise KeelError(
236|                            f"keel: pattern() copy of pocket() at ({px:g}, {py:g}) "
237|                            "falls outside the stock footprint"
238|                        )
239|                elif kind == "slot":
240|                    x1, y1 = params["at"]
241|                    x2, y2 = params["to"]
242|                    moved["at"] = (x1 + i * dx, y1 + j * dy)
243|                    moved["to"] = (x2 + i * dx, y2 + j * dy)
244|                    self._check_xy(*moved["at"], "pattern() copy of slot() start")
245|                    self._check_xy(*moved["to"], "pattern() copy of slot() end")
246|                self._ops.append((kind, moved))
247|        self._seed = None  # a pattern ends the chain; the next pattern needs a fresh feature
248|        return self

250|    def fillet(self, edges="vertical", r=None):
251|        """Round the stock's 4 vertical outer edges; r defaults to the standard 1.0."""
252|        self._guard_open("fillet()")
253|        self._need_stock("fillet()")
254|        if edges != "vertical":
255|            raise KeelError(
256|                f"keel: unknown fillet edges {edges!r}; Keel only rounds 'vertical' "
257|                "(the stock's 4 vertical outer edges)"
258|            )
259|        r = STANDARD_FILLET if r is None else _positive(r, "fillet radius")
260|        if r >= min(self._stock[0], self._stock[1]) / 2:
261|            raise KeelError(f"keel: fillet radius {r:g} does not fit the stock footprint")
262|        self._fillet_r = r
263|        return self

265|    # -- build ------------------------------------------------------------
266|    def _wall_box(self, op):
267|        L, W, T = self._stock
268|        edge, h, t = op["edge"], op["h"], op["t"]
269|        if edge == "north":
270|            return (0, W - t, T, L, t, h)
271|        if edge == "south":
272|            return (0, 0, T, L, t, h)
273|        if edge == "east":
274|            return (L - t, 0, T, t, W, h)
275|        return (0, 0, T, t, W, h)  # west
276|
277|    def _local_top(self, x, y, additives):
278|        """Highest added material covering point (x, y): walls are strips, bosses discs."""
279|        top = self._stock[2]
280|        for kind, p in additives:
281|            if kind == "wall":
282|                L, W, T = self._stock
283|                edge, h, t = p["edge"], p["h"], p["t"]
284|                inside = (
285|                    (edge == "north" and y >= W - t)
286|                    or (edge == "south" and y <= t)
287|                    or (edge == "east" and x >= L - t)
288|                    or (edge == "west" and x <= t)
289|                )
290|                if inside:
291|                    top = max(top, T + h)
292|            elif kind == "boss":
293|                bx, by = p["at"]
294|                if math.hypot(x - bx, y - by) <= p["dia"] / 2:
295|                    top = max(top, self._stock[2] + p["h"])
296|        return top
297|
298|    def _build(self):
299|        L, W, T = self._stock
300|        solid = cq.Solid.makeBox(L, W, T, pnt=cq.Vector(0, 0, 0))
301|        if self._fillet_r is not None:
302|            solid = (
303|                cq.Workplane(obj=solid).edges("|Z").fillet(self._fillet_r).val()
304|            )
305|        additives = []  # (kind, params) of walls/bosses applied so far
306|        for kind, p in self._ops:
307|            if kind == "wall":
308|                x0, y0, z0, dx, dy, dz = self._wall_box(p)
309|                solid = solid.fuse(
310|                    cq.Solid.makeBox(dx, dy, dz, pnt=cq.Vector(x0, y0, z0))
311|                )
312|                additives.append((kind, p))
313|            elif kind == "boss":
314|                x, y = p["at"]
315|                cyl = cq.Solid.makeCylinder(p["dia"] / 2, p["h"], cq.Vector(x, y, T))
316|                solid = solid.fuse(cyl)
317|                additives.append((kind, p))
318|            elif kind == "hole":
319|                clr, (cbd, cbdpth) = KF[p["code"][:-3] if p["code"].endswith("-CB") else p["code"]]
320|                x, y = p["at"]
321|                top = self._local_top(x, y, additives)
322|                cut = cq.Solid.makeCylinder(clr / 2, top + 2.0, cq.Vector(x, y, -1.0))
323|                solid = solid.cut(cut)
324|                if p["code"].endswith("-CB"):
325|                    cb = cq.Solid.makeCylinder(cbd / 2, cbdpth + 1.0, cq.Vector(x, y, top - cbdpth))
326|                    solid = solid.cut(cb)
327|            elif kind == "pocket":
328|                x, y = p["at"]
329|                cx, cy = x + p["L"] / 2, y + p["W"] / 2
330|                top = self._local_top(cx, cy, additives)
331|                box = cq.Solid.makeBox(
332|                    p["L"], p["W"], p["depth"] + 1.0, pnt=cq.Vector(x, y, top - p["depth"])
333|                )
334|                solid = solid.cut(box)
335|            elif kind == "slot":
336|                (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = p["at"], p["to"]
337|                r = p["width"] / 2
338|                seg = math.hypot(x2 - x1, y2 - y1)
339|                if p["depth"] == "thru":
340|                    top = max(
341|                        self._local_top(x1, y1, additives),
342|                        self._local_top(x2, y2, additives),
343|                        self._local_top((x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2, additives),
344|                    )
345|                    z0, zlen = -1.0, top + 2.0
346|                else:
347|                    top = self._local_top((x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2, additives)
348|                    z0, zlen = top - p["depth"], p["depth"] + 1.0
349|                mx, my = (x1 + x2) / 2, (y1 + y2) / 2
350|                ang = math.degrees(math.atan2(y2 - y1, x2 - x1))
351|                bar = cq.Solid.makeBox(
352|                    seg + 2 * r, 2 * r, zlen, pnt=cq.Vector(mx - (seg + 2 * r) / 2, my - r, z0)
353|                )
354|                bar = bar.rotate(cq.Vector(mx, my, z0), cq.Vector(mx, my, z0 + 1), ang)
355|                cutter = bar.fuse(
356|                    cq.Solid.makeCylinder(r, zlen, cq.Vector(x1, y1, z0)),
357|                    cq.Solid.makeCylinder(r, zlen, cq.Vector(x2, y2, z0)),
358|                )
359|                solid = solid.cut(cutter)
360|        return solid.clean()

1|# Keel manual (internal wiki)
2|
3|*Quillon Orbital Works · Structures team · Keel v1.0.0 · QX-2 controlled: on-prem only.*
4|*Fictional company, made for the Forge demo.*
5|
6|Keel is our small internal tool for describing machined satellite parts in Python.
7|A Keel program is a short recipe: start from a base block, add walls and bosses,
8|cut holes, pockets and slots, and finish with exactly one solid. Keel compiles
9|the recipe to a solid model internally, and the Gauge station checks the result
10|against the design request. If you can write the recipe, you can make the part.
11|
12|## 1. Conventions (read this first)
13|
14|All dimensions are millimetres. The datum is the part's **lower-left-bottom
15|corner** at (0, 0, 0): +X points east, +Y points north, +Z points up. Nothing is
16|centred unless the call says so; every position is measured from the datum.
17|
18|The four edges of the base stock have names: **north** (+Y side), **south**
19|(−Y side), **east** (+X side), **west** (−X side).
20|
21|Holes never use raw diameters. Always use a **company fastener code** from
22|table KF below; the Gauge station checks the exact diameters, so a 4 mm drill
23|where a KF-M4 belongs will FAIL the part.
24|
25|Two company standards apply whenever a request says "standard": wall thickness
26|**2.5 mm**, fillet radius **1.0 mm**.
27|
28|Part numbers tell you the family: BRK (bracket), PLT (plate), FRM (frame),
29|STD (standoff), CLP (clip). The `material=` argument (default `AL6061`) is
30|metadata only and never changes the shape.
31|
32|A program has a fixed shape: one `stock()` call first, then features, then
33|`p.finish()` last. `finish()` returns the single solid.
34|
35|## 2. Fastener table KF
36|
37|| Code  | Clearance hole Ø | Counterbore Ø × depth |
38||-------|------------------|-----------------------|
39|| KF-M2 | 2.4              | 4.4 × 2.0             |
40|| KF-M3 | 3.4              | 6.5 × 3.0             |
41|| KF-M4 | 4.5              | 8.0 × 4.0             |
42|| KF-M5 | 5.5              | 10.0 × 5.0            |
43|| KF-M6 | 6.6              | 11.0 × 6.0            |
44|
45|Suffix `-CB` means counterbored from the top face, e.g. `KF-M4-CB`.
46|
47|## 3. API
48|
49|```python
50|import keel
51|p = keel.part("BRK-0412", material="AL6061")
52|```
53|
54|**stock(L, W, T)** — the base block, x in [0, L], y in [0, W], z in [0, T].
55|Exactly one per part, and it must be the first call.
56|
57|```python
58|p.stock(60, 40, 4)
59|```
60|
61|**wall(edge, h, t=None)** — a wall standing on the top face along a named
62|edge (`north`, `south`, `east`, `west`). It sits flush with that edge, runs the
63|full edge length, and rises `h` above the stock top. `t` defaults to the
64|standard wall of 2.5.
65|
66|```python
67|p.wall("north", 25)
68|```
69|
70|**boss(at=(x, y), dia, h)** — a cylinder on the top face centred at (x, y),
71|`h` high.
72|
73|```python
74|p.boss(at=(15, 15), dia=12, h=10)
75|```
76|
77|**hole(code, at=(x, y))** — a through hole, all the way down, using a KF code.
78|A `-CB` code adds the counterbore from the top face.
79|
80|```python
81|p.hole("KF-M4-CB", at=(8, 8))
82|```
83|
84|**pocket(at=(x, y), L, W, depth)** — a rectangular pocket cut from the top
85|face. (x, y) is the pocket's lower-left corner; `depth` must be less than the
86|stock thickness.
87|
88|```python
89|p.pocket(at=(10, 10), L=80, W=60, depth=4)
90|```
91|
92|**slot(at=(x1, y1), to=(x2, y2), width, depth="thru")** — a straight slot with
93|round ends along the centre line from start to end. `depth="thru"` cuts all the
94|way through; a number cuts a blind slot that deep from the top face.
95|
96|```python
97|p.slot(at=(10, 15), to=(40, 15), width=5)
98|```
99|
100|**pattern(nx, ny, dx, dy)** — repeats the LAST feature call in a grid, `nx`
101|by `ny` positions spaced `dx`, `dy` apart. The total is nx × ny instances
102|including the original call's position. Only boss, hole, pocket and slot can
103|be patterned. (A leading text label, e.g. `pattern("hole", 2, 2, 48, 28)`, is
104|accepted and ignored.)
105|
106|```python
107|p.hole("KF-M4", at=(6, 6))
108|p.pattern(2, 2, 48, 28)
109|```
110|
111|**fillet(edges="vertical", r=None)** — rounds the stock's 4 vertical outer
112|edges. `r` defaults to the standard fillet of 1.0. Only `edges="vertical"`
113|exists.
114|
115|```python
116|p.fillet()
117|```
118|
119|**finish()** — returns the part as exactly one solid. Must be the last call;
120|every program ends with `solid = p.finish()`.
121|
122|```python
123|solid = p.finish()
124|```
125|
126|**keel.render(p, path)** — writes an SVG preview of a finished part for the
127|dashboard catalogue. It needs a finished part, so call it after `finish()`.
128|
129|```python
130|keel.render(p, "brk_0101.svg")
131|```
132|
133|## 4. Error messages
134|
135|Keel errors are plain sentences starting with `keel:`. The common ones:
136|
137|- `keel: unknown fastener code 'M4'; holes use company codes KF-M2 ...` — you
138|  used a raw size instead of a KF code.
139|- `keel: stock() called twice; a part has exactly one base block ...` — delete
140|  the second `stock()`.
141|- `keel: hole() called before stock(); every part starts with p.stock(L, W, T)`
142|  — `stock()` must be the first call.
143|- `keel: unknown edge 'top'; edges are named 'north', 'south', 'east' or 'west'`.
144|- `keel: pattern() with no previous feature; call a feature first`.
145|- `keel: render() before p.finish(); finish the part first ...`.
146|

1|"""Build dashboard data for file:// viewing.

3|Reads the company files, rebuilds every example part, writes:
4|  company/dashboard/data.js    (window.QOW_DATA = {...}, loaded via <script>)
5|  company/dashboard/parts/*.svg (isometric SVG previews via keel.render)
6|
7|No network, no server: index.html loads data.js with a <script> tag because
8|Chrome blocks fetch() of local files.
9|
10|The Forge assistant scoreboard reads company/assistant_results.json only if it
11|exists; until the held-out exam exists there is no such file, so the
12|scoreboard is "not measured yet" (never invented numbers).
13|"""
